standards.text: natural hazards originate from geological and hydrometeorological processes and may become disasters depending on the exposure, vulnerability, and capacity of communities;
hazard maps and geospatial information are important tools for identifying areas at risk and supporting disaster risk assessment;
structural and nature-based mitigation strategies can reduce disaster risks and lessen the impacts of hazards on communities; and
disaster risk reduction policies and community preparedness plans help strengthen resilience and reduce disaster impacts.

energy production and consumption influence environmental sustainability, and that the transition to renewable energy sources can help reduce environmental impacts and support sustainable development;
human activities such as excessive groundwater extraction can cause land subsidence and increase risks to communities and infrastructure;
geological conditions and human land-use practices influence slope stability, and appropriate geotechnical interventions can reduce landslide risks; and
sustainable energy systems, responsible land use, and resilient infrastructure contribute to disaster-resilient and sustainable communities.

The learners can analyze hazard maps, disaster records, and risk data to assess disaster risks in local communities. They can evaluate disaster risk reduction strategies and policies and propose evidence-based recommendations that strengthen community preparedness, resilience, and disaster risk management.

The learners can analyze energy, land-use, and geotechnical data to evaluate environmental risks and sustainability challenges affecting communities in the Philippines. They can assess renewable energy options, investigate land stability issues, and propose evidence-based strategies for developing sustainable and disaster-resilient communities.
